name: NutriRoute Cart Vendor Cold-Season Stand Rig
description: Street food vending in GLMZ's Circuit districts means standing in one place for ten to fourteen hours while acid-tinged lake wind comes off the corridor gaps. This rig is built around endurance. The outermost layer is a NutriRoute-branded quilted vest in deep teal with the company's stylized fork-and-circuit-board logo embroidered in white on the left chest — the vest is filled with recycled synth-fiber batting and has a high stand collar that buttons up to the chin. Under the vest goes a long-sleeve henley in heathered charcoal, worn under a NutriRoute-issue apron in waxed canvas the color of dark mustard: bib-style, with a wide front pocket divided into three sections for order slips, a payment scanner, and a cleaning cloth, plus a long side tie that doubles as a hand towel loop. The trousers are straight-leg cargo pants in olive synth-canvas, reinforced at the knees where vendors habitually brace against the cart frame. Footwear is a cushioned steel-toe slip-resistant clog in matte black — chosen for hours of standing on a metal cart platform. A NutriRoute-issue food handler's cap in teal sits flat on the head, and a neck gaiter in heather grey can be pulled up over the lower face during heavy smog advisories. Gloves are thin nitrile over a thin liner glove, swapped constantly through the shift.
functionality: Insulated quilted vest for cold-corridor standing, high wind-blocking collar, waxed canvas apron with divided order-slip pockets, scanner pocket, slip-resistant steel-toe clog for cart platform, smog-rated neck gaiter, nitrile food-handler gloves
what_it_says: The NutriRoute branding makes this person legible to every customer in a three-cart radius — they are the cart, functionally. The mustard apron and teal vest are a color combination chosen by a corporate designer who has never worked a street stand in winter. The vendor has added their own small modifications: a hand-stitched pocket inside the apron bib, a lucky charm pinned to the vest's inner lining.
manufacturer: NutriRoute Franchise Supply Division (vest, apron, cap), Kellow Workwear (trousers), Hollowtread (clogs)
price_range: Φ140–Φ190 (partial company supply, partial personal purchase)
story_hooks: A NutriRoute vendor's divided apron pocket has a false bottom sewn in — they've been passing encrypted data chips to a contact who orders the same item every third day.

During a smog advisory, a vendor pulls up their neck gaiter and is not recognized by a Tier 4 client who had previously arranged to have them fired from a higher-paying position — the client orders food from someone they ruined and never knows.
The hand-stitched inner pocket in the apron bib holds the only copy of a lease agreement for a cart pitch that three different parties are now claiming.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian street-vendor silhouette: compact, layered, heavily branded. The deep teal vest dominates visually, creating a corporate-uniform impression despite the gritty working context. The apron adds a secondary functional layer, and the cargo trousers anchor the outfit to blue-collar practicality. Overall reads as Tier 3 working-class, purpose-built for long shifts in harsh urban microclimates.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and purposefully spacious through the torso to accommodate layering and constant movement; straight-leg trousers with reinforced knees sit comfortably over sturdy slip-resistant clogs. The vest is cut with a high stand collar for neck protection and fits slightly oversized to allow thermal regulation. Apron drapes loose from neck and waist ties.
physical_description.primary_material: Quilted synth-fiber-filled vest (recycled synthetic batting), waxed dark-mustard canvas apron, heathered charcoal merino-blend henley, olive synth-canvas cargo trousers, matte black molded-polymer steel-toe clogs
physical_description.texture: Quilted surface on vest with slight sheen from synthetic fill; waxed canvas apron has a waxy, water-resistant tactile quality with visible weave texture; henley is soft and slightly ribbed; cargo trousers feel sturdy and stiff when new, breaking in to supple wear; clogs have grip-textured sole and smooth molded upper
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant deep teal (vest and cap) contrasted with dark mustard-gold waxed canvas apron; heathered charcoal henley as base layer; olive synth-canvas trousers; matte black clogs; white embroidered NutriRoute logo on chest; heather grey neck gaiter
physical_description.closures: Vest buttons up high stand collar with standard polymer buttons; apron ties at neck and waist; cargo trousers use standard zipper fly with reinforced stitching; clogs are slip-on with molded heel cup; gloves (thin nitrile over liner) are open-hand, swapped frequently
distinctive_features: NutriRoute fork-and-circuit-board logo embroidered in white on left chest
Three-section front apron pocket (order slips, payment scanner, cloth)
Apron side tie doubles as hand-towel loop
Reinforced knee panels on cargo trousers from habitual bracing against cart frame
High stand collar on vest for neck/wind protection
Steel-toe slip-resistant clogs for platform work
Matching teal NutriRoute-issue food handler's cap
Detachable heather grey neck gaiter for smog advisories
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 working-class functional. NutriRoute franchise standardization signals neither aspirational nor desperate — solidly mid-tier service sector.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street-food service sector employee in the GLMZ Circuit districts. The branded uniform marks corporate franchise affiliation; the purposeful design choices (reinforced knees, slip-resistant footwear, thermal layering) signal someone who has done this work long enough to understand the physical toll. Wearing this outfit says: 'I work a 10-14 hour shift standing still in industrial wind; I am equipped and I am reliable.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and practical: vest shows minor pilling at high-friction points (collar, cuffs); apron has faint stains that don't fully wash out (mustard canvas hides them); cargo trousers show creasing at knees and ankles from repeated flex cycles; clogs are scuffed at the heel and toe from constant foot traffic on metal cart platforms; neck gaiter edges are slightly frayed from frequent rolling and unrolling.
